question: Should the paired iOS node expose a first-party `health.summary` capability that sends user-authorized HealthKit aggregates to the configured model provider?
rationale: The architecture supports the proposal, but code inspection cannot authorize a new first-party boundary for sensitive health information, App Store policy, disclosure, and model-provider transmission.

options.title: Sponsor bounded summaries
options.body: Approve one read-only aggregate command with dual opt-in, fixed periods and fields, explicit disclosure, security auditing, and native-device proof.

options.title: Defer HealthKit access
options.body: Keep health information outside the first-party iOS node until the product, privacy, and App Store obligations are prioritized.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded summaries
recommendation.body: Approve one read-only aggregate command with dual opt-in, fixed periods and fields, explicit disclosure, security auditing, and native-device proof.
